## Findings ledger
- [D1.DOC22.F2] Emigh and Riley use Weber to distinguish power held by people from power embedded in language, objects, organizations, and emergent social relations — dim: reader_argument — reader-text-year: Rebecca Jean Emigh and Dylan Riley, 2024 — argument: The text reconstructs Weber as offering an agentive account that must be supplemented by nonagentive forms of power in order to explain how social relations constrain and enable actors — role: A reference point — theme_origin: reader_addition — theme: Marx and Weber as standpoints; meaning, imagined alternatives and class formation — anchor: "But more recent discussions about power have moved beyond the narrowly agentic and subjectivist views embodied in the Weberian and Hobbesian accounts to consider the possibilities of doing and not doing in more detail." — doc: em:QASWYLCG — anchor-b: "Power can be held by people (Weber, 1921/1978, pp. 954, 1112), but also in language (Sewell, 1992, p. 23), material objects (Latour, 1991, pp. 105–110), and organizations (Acker, 1990, pp. 144–146)." — doc-b: em:QASWYLCG — confidence: high — trimmed-anchor: yes

sections_inspected: The Tradition of Elite Theory: From Pareto to Lachmann, pp. 7–18
The Relational Power of Elites and Nonelites, pp. 24–33
scope_outcomes.criterion: A supplied secondary text must make an anchored argument about Max Weber rather than merely name, cite, or list Weber.
scope_outcomes.basis: The chapter explicitly defines Weber’s account of power, characterizes Weberian approaches as narrowly agentic and subjectivist, uses Weber to analyze legitimacy and organizational domination, and incorporates those elements into a broader relational power theory.
limitations: This is one citing chapter and not the authors’ complete reception of Weber.
The assessment records the chapter’s reading of Weber; it does not independently verify all cited Weber editions or passages.

evidence_state.coverage_basis: reader/reviewer report; source bytes do not establish inspection or completeness
blocking_issues: One or more declared finding references lack retained verified evidence
